title: Agentic LLMs, Long‑Context Efficiency, and Emerging Compliance Risks Signal a Structural Shift in AI 2026
core_insight: Agentic LLMs are maturing into autonomous, domain‑specific solutions while breakthroughs in long‑context inference and compliance frameworks reshape AI’s efficiency, regulatory exposure, and market dynamics.

dimension_texts.technology: Agentic frameworks (self‑driving labs, industrial work‑order management) extend LLMs toward autonomous decision‑making, while recent theory papers provide a computational‑complexity view of inference and training‑independent KV‑cache eviction, highlighting limits and optimisation opportunities for longer contexts. Shift toward agent‑centric pipelines combined with training‑agnostic cache management and token‑budget‑driven in‑context learning, emphasizing inference‑stage resource scheduling over model architecture changes. Closing the Analyze-to-Design Gap: An Authorization-Bounded Agent for Self-Driving Laboratories An LLM-Agentic Framework for Intelligent Work Order Management in Industrial Maintenance A Verifier from the Past: Test-Time Compute for Time Series Foundation Models Watch Where You Linearize: Predicting and Correcting Model-Merging Interference LLM Complexity: Towards a Computational Complexity View of Large Language Model Inference Global Importance Estimation for KV Cache Eviction The ROI of Small Examples: Optimizing In-Context Learning Under Token Budgets
dimension_texts.infrastructure: KV‑cache eviction and token‑budget optimisation directly lower memory and compute demand, enabling longer context windows or higher throughput on existing hardware; the complexity upper‑bounds paper aids finer compute planning. No new hardware announcements; efficiency gains stem from algorithmic advances that modestly reduce inference cost in a soft‑hardware co‑design fashion.
